lines.english: Bright moonlight before my bed.
I wonder if it is frost on the ground.
I raise my head and gaze at the bright moon.
I lower my head and think of home.
Sleeping in spring, I do not notice dawn.
Everywhere I hear birds calling.
In the night came the sound of wind and rain.
How many flowers have fallen?
The white sun disappears behind the mountains.
The Yellow River flows into the sea.
To see a thousand miles farther,
climb one more floor.
Goose, goose, goose,
bending its neck to sing to the sky.
White feathers float on green water.
Red feet paddle through clear ripples.
Hoeing grain beneath the midday sun,
sweat falls onto the soil below.
Who knows that the food on our plates
comes from a farmer’s hard work, grain by grain?
Across a thousand mountains, no bird flies.
On ten thousand paths, no human trace remains.
In a lone boat, an old man in a straw cloak,
fishes alone in the snowy, cold river.
Red beans grow in the southern land.
How many branches appear when spring comes?
I hope you gather many of them.
This little thing carries the deepest longing.
